DLO kanban

Each sticker is one job, named in a few words. Hover, tap or tab to a sticker to read more. Generated from docs/KANBAN.md.

Fill color = type
  • world
  • dlo
  • blockchain
  • render
  • tooling
  • test
  • other
Border/badge = status
  • TODO not started yet
  • WIP someone is working on it
  • DONE all finished
What do the card fields mean?
  • type: what part of the world this job is about
  • eli5: the job told in kid words
  • prev: the job that comes just before
  • next: the job that comes just after

(1) Move the species table (`species::SPECIES`) and the biome/zone definitions (`Zone` list, per-zone ground, plants, climate rules) out of Rust code into JSON files loaded at startup, validated by a schema test, with the pinned hashes and the `species_have_biomes` style tests kept green; old saved worlds keep working. (2) For each species replace the single `biomes` list with prioritized PREFERRED and AVOIDED biome lists, split by medium: on land or above water, and below water, each for fresh water and salt water (so a species can prefer fresh surface water, avoid salt water, tolerate deep fresh water, etc). (3) Use these lists so a creature maps a path through biomes to its target biome when migrating or fleeing: the planner scores biome-by-biome transit risk (thirst, hunger, drowning, heat or cold stress, predators) and chooses the safest route, not a straight line. When fleeing, escaping the predator has top priority, so the route may still end in or cross a risky biome where the creature can get hurt or die of starvation, dehydration or drowning; model that as accepted risk, not a bug. Gate ideas (declare in row 1 of docs/metrics/KB-265.jsonl before measuring): death-by-thirst/hunger/drowning per 1000 migration ticks, migration success rate to target biome, flee survival, tick cost p95, same-seed determinism; Habitat and Earth M5 numbers unchanged until deliberately re-pinned. Related: KB-200 (preferred biomes), KB-250/251/256 (swim, aquatic, planners), KB-254 (drowning), KB-188 (flood bound). ITERATION 2 PAIR DESIGN (declared before run): same base/gate/env as 1b, 1460 ticks per arm, sequential; both arms commit a compact per-death table (species, cause, tick, ticks since spawn) to docs/metrics before scratch is deleted. PASS: M1_on <= 0.08 and <= 0.5 x M1_off, each arm >= 40 fresh no-cover spawns; no-harm: starvation, dehydration, killed ON <= 1.25 x OFF + 3; combined env rate ON <= 1.05 x OFF; cold total ON <= OFF; non-old-age deaths ON <= OFF + 3 (net-survival check, new); per-species alive-at-end cap applies only to species with >= 1 ON death (gorilla-style confound removed, declared before the run); killed split target vs non-target species reported. Mechanism read: if non-target killed no longer rises, 1b rise was the lever moving non-target spawns; if target-species killed alone rises, it is survivorship exposure and the lever class closes. ITERATION 2 PAIR RESULT 2026-11-08 (merged, FAIL): valid both arms; M1 OFF 5/50=0.10, ON 0/50=0.00 (met). Killed 31 to 30 (the 1b +13 was the lever moving non-target spawns; scoping fixed it). Caps broken: cold total 41>39, non-old-age 118>111 (corrected from agent's 114), alive-end ladybug 2 vs 7, beaver 4 vs 7, beetle 7 vs 10. Per-death csv committed (docs/metrics/KB-632-iter2-deaths-{off,on}.csv). CLOSED FAIL 2026-11-08: lever reach (5 target cold deaths) is below single-pair noise (~7-10 deaths in untouched causes between two ON runs), so no single pair can give a meaningful no-harm verdict; caps not loosened after reading. Target cold 5 to 0 in both pairs is real but no net survival gain shown (zero-sum cause trade). Lever stays default-off, nothing to roll out. LESSON: absolute death-count caps penalize the arm that keeps more animals alive (ON +16% alive-ticks); use rate-normalized per 1000 alive-ticks caps in future designs. Next: human deaths by cause check (goal: humans first).
